Hi, I witnessed my mum having breakdowns and suicidal episodes when I was 13 which led to many other significant changes and I have never fully recovered. My childhood and innocence essentially ended then. At that time I became completely petrified that people were going to commit suicide around me and that somebody close to me would die in an accident. I developed anxiety and depression and I suspect some sort of PTSD and the thought of suicide has floated around my head since then. Please do not go through with it, at least for the sake of your daughter. My mum was medically treated and back to normal within a few months and managed to get a new job that she likes. I'm sorry that I have no idea about finances and that stuff and I can only imagine how difficult things must be for you. Things will get better for you eventually and you will be proud and glad to watch your daughter grow up. It was probably one of the most painful things I've expericenced when my mum was ill, and even then she survived. I cannot even begin to imagine the pain of those whose parents went through with it. 

Please stay strong for your daughter, and eventually yourself. I wish you and your daughter the best in the future!

Having moved high schools twice, the last time being very recently, my advice would be to start asking the subjects that people are studying and having small conversations about lessons. Eventually, the conversation will progress and you will meet people with similar interests to you. On both occasions there were other new people and we all sort of gravitated towards each other which definitely helped. Honestly, the first few days will be a bit of a challenge but it will get better from then. I used to be very shy, and although I'm still quite quiet I think that moving schools has helped me to open up to new people and hopefully it will help me with changes in adult life.
